notes:
Camera Landing (new)
- An FTP drop your cameras can push into, feeding the watch folder, so clips land and get processed without a card.
- Sony cameras sync over Wi-Fi (Camera Remote SDK). Remote is the default mode so the camera keeps shooting; sync checks every 5 minutes, and each camera can choose its own interval.
- A Wi-Fi clip brings its M01.XML (recovered from inside the MP4), and a clip travels with its sidecars whichever arrives first. A refused login says what the camera refused.

Resolve and timelines
- Resync no longer deletes folders you made in the Media Pool. Sync is additive now: it only moves, bins or removes things Cut Valet created itself.
- Adopt brings the Resolve project's timelines across, read-only until you edit one here. The Adopt sheet shows the clips it is about to adopt, and an adoption can keep running while you do something else.
- Fixed: fifteen b-roll overlays that never reached Resolve while the report said they had. An overlay now moves up a track to keep its audio rather than losing it.
- Fixed: nothing reached Resolve when the Resolve-first hold paused the worker it was waiting on.
- The Catalog's two doors to Resolve open onto one bin, and leave it open.

Analysis
- Describing has one rule for "done", and each describe lane runs its own pass (Snapshot or Temporal description) from its own switch. "All" now really means all, and "Skip the rest" sticks until you re-add the clips, for every lane at once from the queue footer.
- Previews join the Default / None / All dial.
- Two faster engines for the same models: faster-whisper, and 4-bit Qwen.
- Speechmatics is available as a transcription engine.
- A parallel cloud describe lane, and a failed cloud describe fails the clip instead of loading Qwen into the app.
- Rich no longer sits on "Ready" for minutes on long projects; the last clip's preview lane no longer hangs on "picking the best moment".
- Fixed: a Mac with 51 GB free held 1,753 clips because a counter ticked.
- The sidecar now says who is talking and what OCR read in each clip.

Assistant and chat
- The assistant reads a clip's description from the database, so it no longer calls a described clip undescribed. It also tells a stills-only (Snapshot) clip apart from one watched as video.
- Claude Opus 5.5 is the planner's default brain; the GPT-6 family is pickable with its own prices, and every model picker offers what the brain offers.
- A button beside Send leaves a message for when analysis finishes.
- A graphic's length lives in one place, and the AI can change it.

Library, catalog and projects
- Two machines can keep two libraries and fold them together.
- Removed projects leave the catalog and can be removed for good; clips filed into the wrong project can be moved back out.
- The Catalog's "everything ever shot" shows every clip (it showed 300 of 21,776). Analysis and Description columns sort by what they mean.
- Models can be deleted from wherever you see them.

App
- A welcome screen at launch, and a second colour scheme, High readability.
- The tool list is a drag list and tools can live in folders; Tools, Garage and Marketplace are one place.
- When the queue empties it can do something other than say so.
- Fixed: a deleted settings.json used up a licence seat; settings saves raced across processes; the inspector showed UTC times; Show in folder opened Documents; stray wait cursors; Offload died on Start Transfer.
- Many crash and freeze fixes around background workers and the GUI thread.
added: Time of day sync, for lining up a whole day of cameras.
Tech stack, which scans this computer and tunes itself.
Ingest is a page, so several cards can land at once.
The assistant says what it knows, and every line has a switch.
